rows.title: Ground addition by two
rows.why_nontrivial: Tests recursive defining axioms, nested function equality and contextual transport rather than copying a premise or a single defining axiom instance.

rows.title: Compose two additions by one
rows.why_nontrivial: Held-out composition combines nested arithmetic syntax with the entire equality chain. Numeral and subterm pools remain statement-derived.

rows.title: Successor cancellation and transport
rows.why_nontrivial: The target exposes cancellation through injectivity; it is not a substitution of equal successor expressions into a copied successor target.

rows.title: Zero on the left
rows.why_nontrivial: The right-zero defining axiom does not itself say zero on the left. A general argument must apply the declared induction authority.

rows.title: Successor in the first argument
rows.why_nontrivial: This reverses the role of the recursive argument and carries a quantified parameter; it tests transferable conditional fragments and scope handling.

rows.title: Associativity of addition
rows.why_nontrivial: Tests a larger nested equality with several quantified parameters and reusable conditional proof structure.

rows.title: Compose two incidence identifications
rows.why_nontrivial: Combines two distinct instances of the symbolic uniqueness axiom with relational transport. Neither hypothesis is the target.

rows.title: A quantified incidence consequence
rows.why_nontrivial: Moves from one closed incident fact to an arbitrary quantified object and discharged hypotheses, without coordinates or a picture.

rows.title: Existence of a unique joining line
rows.why_nontrivial: Combines existential incidence existence with universal uniqueness; the chosen line must remain a properly scoped witness.

rows.title: A point outside an arbitrary line
rows.why_nontrivial: Tests a global nondegeneracy consequence with an arbitrary line, existential objects and a negative conclusion.

rows.title: Isosceles base angles from literal Hilbert geometry
rows.why_nontrivial: A recognizably geometric theorem needs formal rays/angles/segment congruence and relevant order/congruence axioms. The older SAS/ASA pilot used a different supplied foundation.

status: proposed statements; no actual new runs
